fixes.disposition: fixed: after new-session, start polls `tmux has-session -t =<name>` every 250 ms for --settle-ms (default 3000, at most 60000; exit 2 for out-of-range values) and reports started only if the session was there at every check. Otherwise it exits 2 with the shell-quoted foreground command (cd <root> && TELEGRAM_STATE_DIR=... SM_SCRIPTS_DIR=... claude ... -- '/loop ...'), which contains no token. A shell round-trip of that command was confirmed to give back the exact argv. The tmux stub now models a session that new-session creates (STUB_TMUX_SESSION_DIES=1 simulates a command that exits at once).
fixes.note: A successful real start now takes about 3 s longer, the settle window.

fixes.disposition: fixed: spawn and resume run claude --bg once through runWorkerSession. A failure whose output matches /workspace (is )?not trusted/i (the 2.1.296 stderr is 'Workspace not trusted. Run `claude` in <dir> once and accept the trust prompt, then retry.', evidence 05) exits 2 with: run `claude` once in <dir>, accept the trust prompt, exit, then retry. Nothing is recorded in the ledger. Other failures keep exit 1 and the same message as before. The new setup Step 8 ('Accept workspace trust in each worker repo') lists every worker dir (root, or `repo-dir --repo <key> --raw` per routed repo) and has the operator do this once per routed repo. Start and Verify become Steps 9 and 10. The manager skill treats spawn exit 2 as a setup gap: the item goes back to ready, the CLI message goes to Telegram, the cycle ends recovery-required, and it does not count as a failed attempt.

fixed (prose contract): Telegram rules add 'Never ask in this terminal' (no AskUserQuestion, never end a turn on a question) and 'Telegram unavailable or unpaired': record the question with `ledger set-question <ref>` without `--telegram-message-id`, finish the cycle, end it recovery-required with the summary 'Telegram not paired: run tmux attach -t <name> and pair with /telegram:access pair <code>.', and keep the /loop running. Reconcile begins with 'Unsent questions': every pending question with telegramMessageId null is (re)sent and re-recorded with its message id (askedAt is kept). A worker's question uses the same fallback, with --sender. The Run outcome table lists an unavailable or unpaired Telegram as recovery-required.
